finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the URL starts with "https://". That check does not restrict the host, so an attacker can make the server request internal or link-local HTTPS targets, such as an internal service or cloud metadata behind TLS. axios follows redirects by default, so an attacker-hosted https URL can redirect to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/ and bypass the scheme check. The response size is returned to the caller, and the fetch is a blind or semi-blind oracle for port and host probing.

trace.note: only checks typeof string and startsWith("https://")
axios.get(url) issues the request, following redirects by default
the response byte length is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Scheme prefix check "https://" only. There is no host or IP allowlist or denylist, no DNS resolution or private-range check, no maxRedirects:0 or redirect validation, and no authentication on the route. This guard is insufficient.

verdict.guard_found: none (only typeof string and startsWith("https://") at server.js:11; no auth middleware, no host allowlist, no maxRedirects limit)
verdict.reason: server.js:10-15 takes req.body.avatarUrl, checks only the "https://" prefix at line 11, and passes it to axios.get at line 14 (which follows redirects by default), with no host allowlist or authentication, and returns the response byte length at line 15.
